newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - US is key for Body Shop results.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - US is key for Body Shop results.

text.p: Body Shop International Plc's performance in the United States will be the main focus when the "green cosmetics" retailer reports annual results next Thursday, retail analysts said.

The company, the brainchild of outspoken businesswoman and green-issue activist Anita Roddick, is forecast to boost pretax profits by about 15 percent to around 38 million stg, against 32.7 million last time and raise its dividend about 37 percent to 4.7 pence.
Body Shop made a 1.3 million stg loss in the United States last year and has been working hard to try and get back into profit.
Analysts said they expected the overall results to be broadly in line with the group's Christmas trading statement published in January.
"The U.S. will be doing a bit better, the U.K. will be flat, while Asia will be growing strongly," said one industry analyst, who asked not to be named.
In January Body Shop reported a two percent drop in comparable store sales in the 10 weeks to January 4, but sales were flat in the 44 weeks up to the same date.
Comparable store sales in the U.S. were down three percent in the 44 weeks, the U.K. was flat and Asia was up four percent.

The firm, which has grown from a family business into an international retail brand with some 1,400 stores in around 46 countries, has found life increasingly competitive. Its products made from natural ingredients have spawned whole ranges of 'copy-cat' cosmetics and toiletries both in the U.K. and the United States.

Earlier this year in a break with its policy of not advertising directly, it hired advertising agency Bean Andrews Norways Cramphorn to create a full-blown UK advertising campaign for the first time. The campaign is due to be launched in September.
The group has been experimenting with new-style store designs and in the United States it has used various marketing strategies to try and reverse the downturn.
Body Shop's shares were at 189 pence, up 1/2p at 1050 GMT.
